analysis.investment_thesis: Anup Engineering is a legitimate industrial compounder with 24.5% revenue CAGR, but at 22.4x EV/EBITDA and a negative FCF yield in FY2025, the price already reflects a flawless execution of a multi-year upcycle with zero margin for error. Second-level thinking demands asking what happens if India's capex cycle decelerates — and at this price, the answer is painful.
key_strengths: Genuine revenue compounding — 5Y revenue CAGR of 24.5% with EBITDA expanding from INR 79 Cr to INR 168 Cr, demonstrating operating leverage
Diversified end-markets (oil/gas, petrochemicals, pharma, fertilizers, hydrogen) reduce single-sector concentration risk
Conservative balance sheet historically; Debt/Equity at 0.25 and total debt only INR 32 Cr against INR 636 Cr equity
key_risks: Valuation prices in perfection: at 34.8x P/E and 22.4x EV/EBITDA, any order book slowdown or margin compression triggers a severe de-rating
FY2025 cash flow collapse is alarming — INR 118 Cr net profit yet operating CF of -7 Cr and FCF of -51 Cr signals severe working capital deterioration in a project-based business
Cyclical exposure to oil/gas and petrochemical capex means revenue is vulnerable to any global energy capex retrenchment or domestic private capex slowdown
red_flags: FCF yield is deeply negative (-51 Cr FCF on INR 4,076 Cr market cap = -1.3%) — even FY2024's peak FCF of INR 126 Cr yields only 3.1%, well below my 6-8% threshold
Borrowings surged from INR 34 Cr (FY2023) to INR 158 Cr (FY2025) while cash collapsed from INR 31 Cr to INR 3 Cr — the business is consuming cash despite booking profits
The FY2025 profit-to-cash divergence (INR 118 Cr PAT vs -7 Cr OCF) is a classic project-cycle working capital trap — either receivables are building or advance payments are reversing
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The consensus view on Anup Engineering is straightforward: quality industrial franchise, beneficiary of India's energy transition and refinery capex boom, clean balance sheet. That consensus is not wrong — but it is fully priced at 22.4x EV/EBITDA. The first-level thinker buys quality; the second-level thinker asks what multiple is being paid for that quality and what the downside looks like if the story even slightly disappoints. A process equipment company with cyclical end-markets in oil/gas, fertilizers, and petrochemicals does not deserve the same multiple as a SaaS business. My FCF yield threshold of 6-8% implies fair value closer to INR 750-1,050 Cr market cap on normalized FCF — the stock trades at a 4x premium to that range.

The FY2025 cash flow data is the most concerning signal in this entire dataset. The company reported INR 118 Cr in net profit but generated -INR 7 Cr in operating cash flow. This is not normal — in project-based industrial businesses, this pattern typically means aggressive revenue recognition against uncollected receivables or a reversal of customer advances. Borrowings tripling from INR 34 Cr to INR 158 Cr in two years while cash dropped to INR 3 Cr confirms the company is funding operations through debt, not earnings. Promoter holding at only 40.92% provides limited alignment incentive. In a market where Indian industrial stocks broadly trade at cycle-peak multiples driven by PLI optimism and infrastructure narratives, Anup exemplifies the greed/fear pendulum swinging toward greed. The downside in a moderate capex slowdown scenario — where multiples compress from 22x to 12-14x EV/EBITDA (historical norm for the sector) — implies 40-50% capital loss from current levels. That is not a risk/reward I accept.
